about: Data contracts for the human-context lighting system, revision B. Field names are the canon; examples are illustrative values for one evening in the den (A at the counter, B in the armchair). Status per record: current | partial | proposed | optional. Records changed by the 2026-10-29 corrections pass carry a proposed contract version, which is documentation only: nothing is migrated or deployed. A field that exists only under a pending owner decision is marked as present only under that option, never as required; in the examples an undecided value is null with a status beside it.
frames: room frame: the repo's z_up_metric_floor0 (metres; z up from the floor; x along the room's long axis; origin at the minimum corner). Plans in this sheet set draw +y as 'north' for illustration only; the den's compass bearing is unverified. Bearings are measured clockwise from +y, seen from above. Camera frame: pixels of that camera's native resolution. Times: Unix seconds on one synchronised clock (capture time, not arrival time). Record ids (PersonState's `state_id`: A@1793066610.0 is A's record emitted at 19:03:30.0), `emitted_ts`, `capture_ts`, `depth_ts`, `field_as_of` and every `field_support` time are Unix seconds, written as numbers. Logged event times in Decision, Correction and step logs (`t_exec`, `sent_at`, `since`, verify times, and a log entry's own `ts` or read-back `as_of`) may be written as readable local clock strings (19:03:32.55). Quantities are numbers, with the unit in a sibling `unit` key or in the key name (`_lx`, `_pct`, `_s`, `_k`); an undecided value is null with a status beside it.

records.name: Observation
records.status_note: Detections exist today (Frigate person events; pose and depth placement in the stopped den loop). Capture, arrival and validity times already ride on Lab ledger events (observed_at, available_at, valid_until); a room-frame covariance, transform id and visibility on every observation, and per-joint room geometry (`joints_room`) on keypoints observations, are proposed.
records.proposed_version: proposed minor: `transform_id` narrows to a reference to exactly one `RoomModel.cameras` entry, `<camera_id>@<version>`. Migration note: `den-cam-align@2026-10-18` maps to `den-oak@2026-10-18`. `joint_set`, `joints_room` and `depth_ts` are additive.
records.purpose: One thing one model saw in one sensor reading. The unit everything downstream is built from.
records.producer: K3 Detectors, enveloped by K4 Alignment (also K2 occupancy gate, K6 identity matches)
records.consumers: K4 Alignment → K5 Tracker; K7 Person-state estimator, through `Track.last_obs_ids`; K4 bundle assembly (`PersonBundle.keypoint_series`)
records.rate: per detection; cameras at their frame rate
records.retention: minutes in a ring buffer; kept longer only inside a PersonBundle that is logged

fields.name: joints_room
fields.type: [{j, xyz m | null, cov 3×3 m² | null, status, lift}]
fields.meaning: one entry per joint of `joint_set`, in the room frame: `status` supported | uncertain | unsupported; `lift` stereo | plane:<h> | none. `cov` is A5's Σ_room = R J Σ_meas Jᵀ Rᵀ + Σ_cal. fields.name: room_position

fields.meaning: the model's own confidence

fields.name: visibility

fields.name: validity

records.status_note: A per-person Kalman tracker exists for the LA apartment (greedy assignment; 0 tracks on 2026-09-25); none runs in the den, where person events carry a per-frame slot id. Face recognition is excluded by design at Victoria; people are anonymous tracks with explicit profile binding, and a binding ends when association becomes ambiguous.

records.purpose: One anonymous person followed through time in the room frame, with how sure the system is that it is still the same person.

fields.name: track_id
fields.meaning: anonymous session id (A, B in this sheet); never reused

fields.name: state
fields.meaning: tentative | confirmed | coasting (predicted forward with no recent associated observation) | ended. A coasting track, like an ambiguous one (`association` ambiguous), is an unlocated person for narrow beams: no new narrow beam is aimed near them, and a current spot whose cone meets their widened bound fades to the room's look (A5, A9). Holding the current scene, with no re-aim on stale evidence, never keeps a narrow beam on such a person. Any τ_keep exception is {{dec:tau-keep}} and is never applied as fact; even the exception option never covers a coasting or ambiguous track

fields.meaning: person_state/v1; additive changes only within a major version

fields.name: state_id
fields.meaning: this record's instance id, with `emitted_ts` in full Unix seconds (`A@1793066610.0`). Prose and figures may abbreviate it with the clock time, as in A@19:03:30; records never do. Decision inputs and Correction snapshots reference it

fields.name: emitted_ts
fields.meaning: when the record left K7. It is never a field's support time and never enters an age

fields.name: track_id / identity
fields.meaning: from the Track; identity only if bound

fields.name: position
fields.type: {xyz m, cov 2×2 m² on xy, cov_ts, predicted}
fields.meaning: room-frame floor position (z = 0) from the Track's Kalman estimate. `cov` is stated at `cov_ts` and grows only by the Track's motion model; predicted = true once past the last observation (A7 freshness)

fields.name: working_region

fields.meaning: where the hands and head are working, as a patch on a room surface (glossary: working region)

fields.name: focused_engagement
fields.meaning: none | starting | engaged | ending, and for how long (glossary: focused engagement)

fields.name: visual_demand
fields.meaning: how much detail the task needs: fine work (knife, small print) vs casual. `confidence` is the probability that the band derived from the versioned cut points is correct (a top-label probability); the cut points are {{dec:demand-gates}}

fields.name: attention
fields.type: {head_xyz m, head_cov 3×3 m², head_dir, sd_deg, target, confidence}
fields.meaning: head position (the eye position used by the coordinator's glare and face terms), its covariance at the head's last support, and where the head points (surface, person, screen, none); head pose only, never eye gaze. When the 3D fit and the 2D ratios disagree, `head_cov` is widened to cover both; K7 never grows it with age

fields.name: heading
fields.meaning: body facing, copied from the Track with `Track.heading_as_of`; copying never refreshes it

fields.name: motion
fields.meaning: passing | settling | settled

fields.name: posture
fields.meaning: standing | sitting | crouching | lying | unknown

fields.name: affected
fields.meaning: who else is near and which way they face; the coordinator, not perception, decides whose eyes a light reaches

fields.name: embedding
fields.meaning: learned behavior representation (rN); open-ended, not a class list

fields.name: episodes
fields.meaning: nearest reference episodes; viewer hints are explanations only

fields.name: flags
fields.meaning: association_uncertain | occluded | unfamiliar | prior_leaning | stale:<source>. A record-level summary: per-field status is in `field_support`

fields.name: sources
fields.type: {field: [{origin: rules | student | qwen | prior, ref: obs_id | bundle_id | landmark_id}]}
fields.meaning: what each field rests on, so current evidence, interpretation and a memory prior stay separately inspectable

fields.name: field_as_of
fields.meaning: for position, working_region, attention, heading, posture, motion, visual_demand and focused_engagement: the capture time of the newest accepted evidence, equal to `field_support[f].last_support_capture_ts`. It moves only on accepted evidence, so nothing is presented fresher than its evidence

fields.name: field_support
fields.meaning: for each field the coordinator reads. `support_status`: observed (the newest accepted evidence set the value) | deadband_confirmed (accepted evidence lies within a declared deadband of the published value, so the value is kept and the support time moves) | held_unavailable (no accepted evidence) | held_ambiguous (evidence exists but is not accepted for this person). `hold_reason`: occluded | overlap | association | source_silent | late | refused | transform_invalid | null. A heartbeat repeats each support record as it stands; emission, liveness and occupancy never move a support time, and a new track inherits none. Only the working region's 0.10 m deadband is declared today. The coordinator ages each field as `age_f = t_exec − last_support_capture_ts_f`, with no `T_lat` term; how fresh support reaches it is {{dec:freshness}}

fields.name: interpreter
fields.meaning: rules | student | qwen, and which version produced the learned fields

visual_demand.basis: knife in hand, fine hand motion

records.name: LightState
records.status_note: No camera light measurement runs today; the den RGB camera runs auto-exposure. The camera-measured footprint calibration failed three runs (auto-exposure, ambient light).
records.proposed_version: proposed minor: `anchored` changes meaning (migration note: it is true only when the frame's normalisation version equals k_L's and k_L's calibration passed its checks). `exposure.black_level`, `exposure.normalisation_version`, `room_version`, `rho_status` and `basis` are additive.
records.purpose: What light is in the room right now, from the cameras: estimates on surfaces and at windows, with the exposure facts that make them comparable.
records.consumers: K16 Coordinator, K18 Verify, K7 (so perception knows the system dimmed the room, not the sun)
records.rate: every few seconds from metering frames; on demand for verify
records.retention: summaries logged with every decision and correction. LightState keeps only per-surface summaries, so gold-labelled sessions keep their metering frames, or a per-pixel estimate map with its normalisation version; without them delivered service at R_eval is unknown. Whether to retain them is {{dec:recording-retention}}

fields.name: ts
fields.meaning: capture time

fields.name: camera_id
fields.meaning: which camera

fields.name: room_version
fields.meaning: the RoomModel version whose camera scale k_L and reflectances converted these estimates

fields.name: exposure
fields.meaning: the facts that turn pixels into the normalised reading C(s), in normalised counts (nc): the mean over unclipped, unmasked pixels of m·(raw − b)/(t·G), with t the exposure in ms, G the analogue gain multiplier (not ISO; if only ISO is known, G = ISO/ISO_base with the base recorded), b the black level for that gain and m a fixed linear channel weighting with a matrix id. Changing any of these makes a new `normalisation_version`; only linear values count

fields.name: anchored
fields.meaning: true only when the frame's `normalisation_version` equals that of the camera's k_L and k_L's CalibrationRecord passed its checks (the round trip and independent held-out card and meter checks in lux). Otherwise the estimates are relative and no absolute lux claim is made

fields.name: surface_estimates
fields.meaning: camera estimate of light arriving at each visible surface, Ê(s) = π·k_L·C(s)/ρ_s for matte surfaces, converted with `room_version`'s k_L and ρ. `rho_status` assumed | measured; `basis` measured | fallback_patch | prior. A `fallback_patch` or `prior` estimate never counts as delivered service

fields.name: window_daylight
fields.meaning: daylight tracked at the windows, as a number with its unit

fields.name: sun
fields.meaning: computed from location and time

fields.name: blinds
fields.meaning: from vision or smart blinds

fields.name: residual
fields.meaning: measured minus predicted for the actual resulting state (Decision.applied_scene at the current hold revision): what neither the light model nor daylight explains, such as something moved or someone in the way. A held channel is never explained as scale drift

fields.name: frame

fields.name: surfaces

fields.name: guardrails
fields.type: per offset: level_factor [lo, hi] ×; mired_shift [lo ≤ 0, hi ≥ 0] mired; contrast_shift [lo, hi] log₂; fixed: [names of targets or rules no preference may move]; per-target minimums such as pool_ratio_min
fields.meaning: the range preferences may move each target, as explicit relative ranges: `level_factor` as a factor, `mired_shift` in mired with positive = warmer, `contrast_shift` in log₂. `fixed` lists the targets and rules no preference may move, and a per-target minimum such as cooking@1's `pool_ratio_min` is a floor no preference may push below (A10). records.status_note: The virtual den stores declared preferences; learning them from corrections, and the separate tighten-only comfort limits, are proposed.

records.purpose: How this household, or a bound person, likes a need met: offsets on the look's targets, with how sure we are; and, kept apart, comfort limits that corrections can only tighten.
records.producer: K15 Preference model (offsets, from Corrections attributed to the preference link); K20 attribution (comfort_limits, tighten-only, from AR3 and AR10 only)

A colour observation is the light's reported colour temperature after the change (readback), not measured spectrum; a brightness-only change gives none. While colour parameters are unvalidated, `mired_shift` stays 0 and only level is learned

records.name: Decision
records.status_note: The lighting brain logs rule decisions and accepts overrides (change, aim, undo, redo); the virtual den binds corrections to the run and decision; den_lighting already re-checks its revision and the light's current target before each call. Candidates, requested and applied scenes, recipients, predictions and verify are proposed.
records.proposed_version: proposed major (v2): `scene` becomes `requested_scene` plus `applied_scene`; `predicted`, `recipients` and `verify` are for the actual resulting state; the hold set, revisions, actuator state, step log, `hard_conflicts` and the policy tags are new. Option-dependent fields are present only under their pending option: `held[].direction`, `held[].footprint` and `hold_limited` under P1–P3, `held[].changer_track` under P3 ({{dec:compensation}}); `safety_override` under S1/S2 ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}).
records.purpose: Everything needed to explain a lighting change later and to attribute a correction to it.
records.producer: K16 Coordinator (inputs, targets, candidates, requested_scene); K17 Actuation (applied_scene with the step log, skipped, status); K16 via K13 (predicted and recipients for the actual resulting state, once K17 reports, whatever the status); K18 Verify (verify)
records.consumers: K20 Attribution, K23 Evaluation (targets, recipients and verify points are diagnostics there, never the evaluation region), replay, people reading the log

fields.name: decision_id / ts
fields.meaning: identity and time

fields.name: trigger
fields.meaning: person_state change | light residual | time of day | correction | hold change (a hold opened, replaced or ended)

fields.name: policy / actuator_domain / actuation
fields.meaning: which policy and version wrote it (a den_lighting command recorded at rung 0 is `den_lighting@<version>` and counts as no decision for attribution); the actuator domain; `actuation` shown | shadow | replay | synthetic. Corrections per hour are filled only from `shown` decisions; a virtual-den decision is synthetic

fields.name: inputs
fields.meaning: PersonState `state_id` values (each with its `field_support`), light_state id, room, fixture and light model versions, look and preference versions applied (with the comfort_limits version), coordinator, router and recipient-rule versions, `body_envelope` {version, parameters, parameters_status}, the incumbent's mode, place_memory version if a prior re-ranked anything, and the entries below. A log may add `person_state_display`, the clock abbreviation (A@19:03:30) for readers. The envelope parameters are {{dec:envelope-parameters}}, so `parameters` is null with `parameters_status` until decided

fields.name: inputs.field_support
fields.meaning: the per-field support each PersonState carried when the plan was made, keyed by `state_id`: `last_support_capture_ts` in Unix seconds and `support_status` observed | deadband_confirmed | held_unavailable | held_ambiguous, as in `PersonState.field_support`. Every body field is aged from it to `t_exec`

fields.name: inputs.hold_set
fields.type: {revision, held[{entity_id, channels, pinned {level_pct, cct_k, aim, source}, since, cause, lifetime}]}
fields.meaning: the HA-local hold set K20 and K17 keep, copied in at the decision's revision (an integer: revision 7 before c-190405 and 8 after it in the example). `pinned` is the held light's read-back state as numbers, `source: read-back`. Present only under P1–P3 ({{dec:compensation}}): `held[].direction` and `held[].footprint`; under P3 also `held[].changer_track`

fields.name: inputs.revisions
fields.meaning: the revisions the plan was made under; the mode revision moves on occupancy, gaming, enable, resume and hold expiry, as den_lighting's controller revision does

fields.name: inputs.actuator_state
fields.type: per channel {on, level 0–1, v_hat 0–1, cct_k, aim, motion_status, source, as_of}
fields.meaning: the actual state: `level` is the commanded fraction and `v_hat` (v̂) the output fraction; `motion_status` settled | moving | stopped | unknown; `as_of` is when the value was last read back from the light, not when a poll or connection last succeeded

fields.name: inputs.t_exec
fields.type: per new, changed or kept channel: s, or null + `<channel>_status`
fields.meaning: t_exec = max(t_settle, t_chk + T_chk + T_react), the horizon every body field is aged to (`age_f = t_exec − last_support_capture_ts_f`); for a kept channel t_settle = t_chk. T_chk and T_react are {{dec:freshness}}, so a kept channel's t_exec is null with a status that gives the formula. In the example F1's spot settles at 19:03:32.55 as logged (dark move 19:03:30.05–19:03:30.55, then the 2 s fade), so the head support ages at t_exec are 2.75 s for A and 7.65 s for B

fields.name: targets
fields.type: per person {surface_id, lx, cct_k, note} / per layer
fields.meaning: what the look and the needs asked for, after preferences: the coordinator's own targets, which evaluation reads only as diagnostics. Each is a target to validate

fields.name: candidates
fields.meaning: the alternatives the optimizer weighed: `cost` is the weighted total (a number) and `why` says why each was chosen or lost (`chosen`, optionally followed by its reason, or `rejected: <reason>`)

fields.name: requested_scene
fields.type: per channel {level, cct_k, target_cct_k, clip_reason, aim}
fields.meaning: the solver's output, with held channels at their pinned read-back values. `cct_k` is the commanded value after the guardrail clamp and the `Fixture.channels[].cct_range_k` clip; `target_cct_k` is the value before the clip, with `clip_reason`. A clip is not a delivery fault

fields.name: applied_scene
fields.type: per channel {status, readback {level, cct_k, aim}, aim_status, aim_source, steps[]}
fields.meaning: the actual resulting state of every channel in the decision, whether sent, dropped or held, from `readback` (`cct_k` as reported, not measured spectrum). `status` sent | held | superseded | stopped | repaired | completed_after_check | failed; a channel whose requested value was already in effect is listed with status sent and empty `steps[]`, because nothing went out for it. `aim_status` settled | moving | stopped | unknown; `aim_source` commanded | encoder | unknown, commanded while `Fixture.gimbal` declares no position readback. `steps[{kind, revisions, sent_at, result {status, at, readback}, reason, checks}]` logs K17's step check before every send, fade, move, retry and callback (a Hue bulb today has one send, then readback; an engineered spot has fade-out, move, settle and fade-in, each a step): a held light or a newer owner drops the old plan's remaining steps; after an unrelated revision change, or a step that would finish after its logged t_exec, a step goes out only after fresh checks, and one that cannot be checked on the Pi fails closed ({{dec:local-completion}}). No superseded timer, retry or callback resends an old value; a spot cut short may stay dark; a stop is never a restore. A step logged as sent without passing the check fails replay

fields.name: skipped
fields.meaning: each channel that was not sent, with why and the hold it met

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: superseded if no step went out after a revision change, partial if some did; kept_current if no fresh plan arrived within the deadline D ({{dec:resolve-deadline}}). There is no silent partial send

fields.name: hard_conflicts
fields.type: [{constraint, held_channel, track, eye_or_envelope, G_hi, limit, model_status}]
fields.meaning: a held light that alone breaks a hard constraint (the hard glare limit, the head-and-shoulder cone, an eye box). Every hard constraint stays on for the free channels, which may not raise their part of a conflict; nothing is relaxed silently. What happens to the held light itself is {{dec:manual-vs-safety}}

fields.name: hold_limited
fields.meaning: present only under P1–P3 ({{dec:compensation}}): points where a footprint bound leaves the decision's own target unmet. The candidate's diagnostic at its own target, never a delivery miss; evaluation recomputes it at the evaluation region

fields.name: safety_override
fields.meaning: present only under S1/S2 ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}): a logged limit of a held light, given with notice

fields.name: recipients
fields.type: per applied channel {served[], exposed[], layers[], targets[{target_id, kind: task | eye | layer, track_id | layer, share, lx}]}
fields.meaning: share_{c,i} = B_ic·V_c(i)·v_c/E_i with holds pinned, first on the requested scene, rewritten for the actual resulting state when K17 reports. `served`: tracks whose task share is at least s_serve; `exposed`: tracks whose conservative eye envelope at t_exec gets non-negligible predicted eye luminance (a held head never drops a person from it); `layers`. Each share carries the LightModel version and an interval; s_serve and s_aff are {{dec:attribution-thresholds}}. A runtime share at the coordinator's own targets: it is not service and never scores

fields.name: predicted
fields.type: {surfaces {point: E, unit}, eyes [{track_id, channel, G, G_hi, limit, model_status, t_exec, support_age s}], eyes_note}
fields.meaning: what the light model expects for the actual resulting state (requested = applied when everything was sent). Eyes are predictions only: G_hi is the upper bound over the conservative eye envelope at t_exec, with each field grown from its support, plus model uncertainty; `model_status` unvalidated | validated@version; `support_age` = t_exec − the head's last support, in seconds. While no glare model or numeric limit exists, G, G_hi and limit are null and `eyes_note` says what is predicted (in the example: well under the limit at A, about 0 at B)

fields.name: verify
fields.type: {ts, light_state, anchored, unit, points[], spill[], increments[], not_verified[], tolerance, tolerance_status, within_tolerance, explanation}
fields.meaning: against the prediction for the actual resulting state, from the first frame after the last step that went out has settled (frames taken mid-fade or mid-move are not verify frames). Light values are numbers in `unit` (lx when anchored); `residual` and `tolerance` are relative, (measured − predicted) / predicted. `points[{point_id, kind, status: within | outside | unverifiable | prior_only, camera_estimate, residual}]` are surfaces only. `spill[{track_id, region, measured_after, spill, status}]` with spill_j = max(0, E_j − (T_j^hi + a_j)) is reported and never fires AR1. `increments[{point_id, measured_change, predicted_change, status}]` compares the measured change Ê_after − Ê_before with the light model's own predicted change E_after − E_before (the contribution of the channels the decision changed, never predicted-after minus measured-before), both signed numbers; only it and the served-region level check feed AR1. `not_verified` lists eye ids: no camera measures glare at an eye. A held channel is never explained as scale drift

records.name: Correction
records.status_note: Home posts overrides with reasons (change, aim, undo, redo) to the lighting brain, which pauses that virtual fixture; the virtual den saves feedback verdicts bound to the run and decision; den_lighting detects manual changes on the four real Hue bulbs from HA Context ids and service calls and holds each changed bulb on its own; LA's Living Lights detects manual touches. The context snapshot, the action grouping, whose light it was and the attribution are proposed.
records.proposed_version: proposed major (v2): `change` becomes `changes[]`, one Correction per human action; `who` narrows to the single track within reach; `action`, `affected`, `whose_light`, `reason`, `hold` and `attribution.comfort` are new; rules become AR0–AR11 (AR10 = comfort, AR11 = abstain). Present only under P1–P3 ({{dec:compensation}}): `hold.direction` and `hold.footprint`; present only under S1/S2 ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}): `override_contested`.

records.consumers: K16 Coordinator and K17 Actuation (the hold, through the hold set), K15 Preference model, K7 thresholds and hysteresis, K22 Teaching queue (only if E1 holds), K23 Evaluation

fields.name: correction_id / ts
fields.meaning: identity and time. `ts` is the action's capture time, written `c.capture_ts` in K20's pseudocode (A11): the capture time of the action's last change, fixed when the settle window closes. Holds, attribution and comfort are all evaluated at it

fields.name: source
fields.meaning: wall switch | app | voice | scene button

fields.name: ha_context
fields.meaning: how the system tells its own changes from a person's

fields.name: action
fields.meaning: how the reports were grouped into one human action (the reported levels it merged, in order): one HA context, or one physical control (scene button, group, voice) within the settle window. Per-entity debouncing never splits an action, and the action is the unit corrections per hour count

fields.name: changes
fields.meaning: every entity the action changed, with the read-back state before and after as numbers (only the keys that apply); a scene button that sets four bulbs is one Correction with four changes

fields.name: affected
fields.meaning: the task (surface) targets the change moved by at least s_aff ({{dec:attribution-thresholds}}), written on every affected track's Episode; eye exposure is read only by the comfort rule AR10

fields.name: whose_light
fields.meaning: room | shared | changer | another | layers | unknown, tested in that order, from the recipients of the deciding Decision or, with none, from the light model in force; reach is tested on support-aged position bounds. A shared, room-wide or unknown light learns nothing about people (AR11)

fields.name: decision_id / since_decision_s
fields.meaning: the latest Decision that set the entity within T_steady, and how soon after. If that writer was den_lighting, attribution treats it as no decision, and an older coordinator Decision is never used in its place. If the decision was cut short, attribution reads the actual state at the change; if it was still running, {{dec:mid-execution}} decides between judging against its requested scene and abstaining

fields.name: who
fields.meaning: the single track within reach of the control, else null (nobody or two people within reach, an app user with no bound profile, or voice naming only the room); an app user names a track only through a bound profile. A track flagged association_uncertain stays named, and the case then goes to AR2

fields.name: reason
fields.type: {kind: glare | too_bright | too_dim | colour | other | none, via: app | voice}
fields.meaning: optional explicit report; a glare report is tested first, before delivery. Which report channels exist is {{dec:comfort-policy}}

fields.name: snapshot
fields.meaning: PersonState `state_id` values with their `field_support` (as in `Decision.inputs.field_support`), which the comfort test ages from; LightState references: the frame the decision read, its verify frame and the first frame after the change has settled, which is appended when attribution reads it (ls-190409 in the example); the decision's applied scene; the actual state at the change, with any step in progress; the holds in force before it (`holds_before`, a hold set `{revision, held[]}` as in `Decision.inputs.hold_set`); the policy in control (`policy`), den_lighting's mode with its revision (`mode`) and the hold's end rule (`hold_end_rule`)

fields.name: hold
fields.type: {entity_id, channels, pinned {level_pct, cct_k, aim, source}, since, lifetime, hold_set_revision, ended}
fields.meaning: the hold this change opens or replaces at capture, whatever the attribution: it pins every channel of the entity at its read-back state (`pinned`, as numbers, `source: read-back`) and drops older plans' remaining steps, timers, readback checks and retries for it. `hold_set_revision` is the hold set's new integer revision (8 after c-190405, from 7). Fields the person did not set come from {{dec:unset-hold-fields}}. The lifetime is den_lighting's today: outside a game, until 120 s of vacancy after the later of vacancy start and the latest touch; during a game, until the game ends (game-time vacancy turns held bulbs off without ending their holds; game exit clears every hold); or resume_automatic. Changing it is {{dec:hold-lifetime}}. Whether a hard safety limit may still limit a held light is {{dec:manual-vs-safety}}

fields.name: override_contested
fields.meaning: present only under S1/S2 ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}): true when the action raises a light that a safety override (`Decision.safety_override`) is limiting at `ts`. It is tested right after an explicit glare report; a contested correction goes to hand sorting, never to AR3–AR9, and the override re-applies while the conflict lasts. Under S0 there are no safety overrides and the field is absent, not false

fields.name: attribution
fields.type: {link: p} + rule | abstained + reason | hand_sort; comfort {status, basis, G_hi_over_limit, G_hi_over_limit_status}
fields.meaning: perception | need | preference | delivery | execution, with the rule (AR0–AR11; AR10 = comfort, AR11 = abstain) that decided, or abstained with its reason (shared, room, unknown, unknown_changer; mid_execution only under the pending abstain option), or sent to hand sorting (override_contested, only under S1/S2). `comfort` {status: reported | suspected | predicted_clear | unknown, basis, G_hi_over_limit} is computed on each person's eye envelope aged from its support in the snapshot to `ts`. `G_hi_over_limit` is the number G_hi / limit, a prediction only, never a measured glare value; while no glare model or numeric limit exists it is null with `G_hi_over_limit_status`. Comfort is never learned as taste

fields.name: updates
fields.meaning: the value before (`delta.from`) and after (`delta.to`) as numbers, with `delta.n`, the number of corrections behind it; only what the firing rule permits (A11's permission table): AR3 and AR10 only tighten comfort limits, AR11 changes nothing about people, and comfort is never learned as taste

fields.name: baseline
fields.meaning: the historical activity figures are three dated facts, not a baseline: session 0dc34636 (den-facts-6, about 1 s validity) gave 16–19% coverage and about 0.51 answered accuracy, mostly against Qwen-proposed labels; the facts-bound validity replay gave 43–49% coverage with accuracy not recomputed; the independently labelled subset is only the computer interval (computer_work 0.07/0.00), also hit by a stale-device bug fixed afterwards. Every accuracy is reported with its coverage on the same accepted seconds and validity version

fields.name: gold_set
fields.type: {n_intervals, refreshed, label_version, hash, regions {marked, uncertain, missing}, R_eval[], tau_R, tau_R_status, n1 {fixture {version, hash}, labels {version, hash}}}
fields.meaning: owner-confirmed intervals, never model-made labels, with the worked-patch marks that define each `R_eval` (below), drawn from the hands and the worked object, never from where the light falls. The set, geometry included (every `R_eval` outline), is versioned by `label_version` and hashed into `hash` before any candidate output is opened; a region has no freeze time or hash of its own, and a mark redrawn after hashing is not used. `regions` counts the marks of its fine and casual intervals. For N1 and N2, `n1` holds N1's input fixture (per-frame person boxes, one constant id, a static surface map) and its blind labels as two separately versioned, hashed artifacts; the fixture is a fixed input, not gold. τ_R is {{dec:reference-geometry}}, so `tau_R` is null with `tau_R_status`; the missing-geometry rule is pending with it, and marking every interval or a sample is {{dec:labelling}}

fields.name: R_eval
fields.type: {surface_id, outline, source: gold_mark | task_spec, label_version, placement_sd}
fields.meaning: the evaluation region R_eval(e, t) of one gold need episode, a patch on a named surface: `outline` is its outline on `surface_id` in room-frame metres. `source` is `gold_mark`, the owner's blind mark of the worked patch, or `task_spec`, on a staged session only, a task location written into the protocol before recording. `label_version` names the label set that holds it; that set, geometry included, is versioned and hashed in `gold_set` before any candidate output is opened. `placement_sd` (cm, in the surface plane) is the annotator's stated placement uncertainty, plus the registration bound when the mark is projected from another camera; it is tested against τ_R, and a mark beyond τ_R is uncertain. A mark covers only the sub-interval it was drawn for, and each person has their own: another person's patch on the same surface never stands in. Never a PersonState working region, a Decision target, `Decision.recipients`, a verify point, a fallback patch or anything else a scored arm produced; the candidate's region never enters the τ_R test

fields.name: per_link
fields.type: {tracking, working_region_cm, engagement, visual_demand {ece, fine_recall, false_fine_rate, coverage_per_band, episodes_per_band}, attribution {kappa_six_class, update_precision {changer, layers}, forced_update_rate, abstained, shared}, camera_scale {round_trip, held_out_error_lx}, …}
fields.meaning: checks for each link. `tracking`: id switches per crossing, silent swaps, IDF1; `working_region_cm`: median and p90 error; `engagement`: onset delay, early-off seconds per hour, F1. `visual_demand`: `fine_recall` (with its paired session-bootstrap interval, at the level in `interval_level`; {{dec:promotion-margins}}), `false_fine_rate`, `coverage_per_band`, the confusion matrix with 'no answer', `episodes_per_band` (and sessions per band), and `ece` with its bin count; competence and calibration are both gated ({{dec:demand-gates}}). `attribution`: `kappa_six_class`, `update_precision` per path (changer, layers), `forced_update_rate`, and the `abstained` and `shared` shares, with coverage and abstention by stratum. `camera_scale`: the round trip and the held-out error in lux, lower is better

fields.name: end_to_end
fields.type: {occupied_hours, corrections_per_occupied_hour, rescues_per_h, missed_service_per_h, unserved_need_min_per_h, time_to_good_light_s {median, p90}, false_triggers_per_h, service {served_delivered, served_predicted, missed_rescued, missed_unrescued, unknown {no_gold, geometry, unverifiable, no_frame}, hold_limited_min, hold_limited_status, safety_limited_min, safety_limited_status}, delivered_coverage, rev, rev_status}
fields.meaning: the outcome people feel, scored at R_eval: delivered service from retained metering frames with one frozen K11 version; predicted service only where R_eval was unverifiable for a reason the arm did not cause, in its own column and never gated; unknown, with its reason, stays in coverage's denominator. `service` counts gold need episodes; `delivered_coverage` = served_delivered / all episodes, unknown included. `missed_service_per_h` is the needs left unserved (measured where the owner marked the work), (missed_rescued + missed_unrescued) / occupied_hours; a rescue is a person turning a light on or up because the floor was not met at R_eval (A13). `unserved_need_min_per_h` is the minutes of gold need with reference geometry that were not delivered-served at R_eval, per occupied hour; it is gated beside missed service and delivered coverage (A13 Gate 3). Under P1–P3, everyone else's `hold_limited` minutes count inside it ({{dec:compensation}}). `safety_limited_min` exists only under S1/S2 ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}): the minutes in which a safety override dimmed the changer's own region below F(c), kept in coverage's denominator and left out of `unserved_need_min_per_h`; elsewhere it is null with `safety_limited_status`. The candidate's region, targets, recipients, verify points and fallback patches never score. `hold_limited_min` exists only under P1–P3 ({{dec:compensation}}), so elsewhere it is null with `hold_limited_status`. REV is null with `rev_status` 'undefined (0 system changes)', never 0. Corrections count one per human action, over `occupied_hours` (the sum of `exposure`) per arm and stratum, with the occupancy rule, the allocation unit, the rate ratio ± CI and φ̂ from a quasi-Poisson model with a log-exposure offset over blocks. The delivered statistic is {{dec:delivered-statistic}}; floors and the quiet window are {{dec:service-floors}}

fields.name: region_diagnostics
fields.meaning: the candidate's region against the owner's mark, per episode; reported, never gated and never in a numerator. Replacing the candidate's regions leaves every service outcome unchanged

fields.name: shadow
fields.meaning: candidate vs the live (shown) policy on the same moments, in the same actuator domain

fields.name: comparator
fields.meaning: at rung 9, the frozen den_lighting incumbent (manifest 1.0.4: VACANCY_SECONDS 120, gaming at 38/255 warmest, resume_automatic, read statically), its shown Hue scenes (`actuator_domain` hue-den-4, `kind` shown) through one rung-8 LightModel version, which is null with a status until it exists. The candidate's anticipation and stability rates are replay surrogates against candidate floors fixed before the run, never differences (the incumbent scores 0 and 1 by construction). The virtual-den study is `kind` synthetic (virtual-den-4) and never counts toward rung 9 or promotion

fields.name: exposure
fields.type: {per_session [{session_id, occupied_h, occupancy_source, mode_stratum, corrections}], occupied_h_total, corrections_total, phi_hat, phi_hat_status}
fields.meaning: per-session exposure, from rung 0's log: occupied hours, the source that decided occupancy, and den_lighting's mode as the stratum, with the corrections counted one per human action. φ is fitted from these counts by a quasi-Poisson model with a log(occupied_h) offset; until a run exists `phi_hat` is null with a status

fields.name: replay
fields.meaning: replay reproduces every requested and applied scene from the logged inputs, hold sets and step log; paced replay measures each request's service time at the declared single-track cadence (one request per 4 s), and only capture scheduling is emulated

fields.name: coverage
fields.type: {intervals, people, rooms, conditions, eval_region {with_geometry, uncertain, missing, by arm and stratum}}
fields.meaning: what the run actually covered, so a pass is not read beyond it; if missing-geometry rates differ between arms, the service comparison is insufficient, not passed

fields.name: intervals
fields.type: per metric: {metric, live, candidate, better, unit, improvement, interval, interval_level, interval_level_status, delta, delta_status, result}
fields.meaning: `improvement` is the oriented improvement Δ_m = s_m·(m_candidate − m_live), with s_m = +1 if `better` is higher and −1 if lower, so positive is better, in `unit`; `interval` is its interval from a paired bootstrap over whole held-out sessions. Non-inferiority passes iff the lower bound > −δ_m, superiority iff it is > 0; a candidate only replaces the live policy if no part it touches is worse, beyond a margin set in advance. The interval convention (two-sided 95% recommended, pending) is {{dec:promotion-margins}}, so `interval_level` is null with `interval_level_status`. `result` says in words what the interval means for the gate

fields.name: intervals[].delta
fields.type: δ_m ≥ 0, absolute, in the metric's unit; null + delta_status
fields.meaning: the pre-registered margin, frozen with the gate before the run, one per gated metric. This is the record's margins field and the only place δ_m is stored; there is no separate margins table. Every δ_m is {{dec:promotion-margins}}, so `delta` is null with `delta_status` until it is set

fields.name: sample_gate
fields.type: per class and per band: passed | below gate
fields.meaning: too few examples means no score (hold), not a good score; for demand, per band ({{dec:demand-gates}})

fields.name: scored_by
fields.meaning: which label source scored it; weak labels never score

fields.name: canary
fields.type: {share, rollback_trigger, block_schedule, allocation_unit, mode_strata, block_reset, handback, washout}
fields.meaning: how much live traffic a promoted model gets first and what rolls it back. The block reset writes the incumbent's normal snapshot, then calls resume_automatic, then checks the status sensor. Game-time strata and washouts are {{dec:gaming}}. Rollback fires on free channels predicted over a hard glare limit or raising their part of an open hard_conflict, or on glare reports per hour above the bound; under S1/S2 also on a held-light conflict open past its deadline ({{dec:manual-vs-safety}}). No rollback cites a measured glare value

fields.name: decision
fields.meaning: the gate's result on a promotion run. N2 never promotes: it writes `verdict` (feasible | not_feasible | insufficient) instead

fields.name: verdict
fields.meaning: N2's result (sheet A14), written in place of a promotion decision: nothing is promoted or changed in the loop, and an unmet sample gate gives insufficient, never a relaxed threshold. When N1 and N2 run is {{dec:need-test-order}}

records.name: CalibrationRecord
records.status_note: Tape and scan workflows record their source today; probe, fit and card-and-meter methods are proposed. No camera scale has been measured.
records.proposed_version: additive: method `meter`, `inputs` and `checks`, and K11 as a reader of the camera scale.
records.purpose: One calibrated parameter with where it came from, so the system always knows how much to trust each number.
records.consumers: RoomModel, Fixture, LightModel; K11 Light measurement reads k_L through RoomModel.cameras[].photometric
records.retention: versioned; manual values are kept as the test set for automatic ones

fields.name: parameter
fields.meaning: e.g. F1.orientation_calibration.anchor_deg

fields.name: value / unit
fields.type: number, or an enum for a categorical parameter (for example order: cw | ccw)
fields.meaning: the value; a categorical value has no unit. `unit_note` may state the convention, such as the bearing frame

fields.name: method
fields.meaning: assumed | manual (the owner's own call, such as a zone named in the inspector) | tape | scan | probe | fit | from-use | meter (a grey card plus one lux-meter reading); a combination, such as probe + fit, is written with +

fields.name: residual / confidence
fields.type: number, or a map of numbers per option for a categorical parameter
fields.meaning: how well the fit explains the data, as numbers with the unit in the key name (for example `residual_deg_rms` over `n_zones`, `confidence_deg_1sigma`). For a categorical parameter the residual is given per option (order: `residual_deg_rms` {ccw, cw}) and the confidence is the margin between the best two (`confidence_deg_margin`)

fields.name: inputs
fields.type: {normalisation_version, rho_card, E_meter_lx, C_card_nc, exposure, clipped_frac, illuminant}
fields.meaning: for method meter: k_L = ρ_card·E_meter/(π·C_card), in (cd/m²)/nc, under the frame's normalisation version (for example `meter-norm/v1`), from one grey card plus one meter reading at the card; the other meter points and later days are held back as checks. `clipped_frac` is the card's clipped fraction

fields.name: checks
fields.meaning: the round trip is a software identity check through K21, then the production K11 path: C_card 100 nc, ρ_card 0.18, E_meter 174.533 lx must give k_L 0.100 (cd/m²)/nc, L 10.0 cd/m² and Ê back 174.533 lx. Held-out checks use independent card and meter points and days against a tolerance fixed in lux before the run ({{dec:photometry-commissioning}}). A common scale cancels from relative residuals and camera-fitted relative-error scores, so those can neither be corrupted by a scale error nor detect it; absolute lux values and errors, fixed physical thresholds and independently scaled physics or datasheet terms do scale. Rung 7 needs both the round trip and independent held-out card and meter checks in lux, as future qualification

fields.name: ts / version / supersedes
fields.meaning: history; `supersedes_method` and `supersedes_value` keep the method and value of the version this one replaces

fields.name: vs_manual
fields.type: delta, a number + vs_manual_unit; or same | differs
fields.meaning: difference from the owner's manual value, while both exist: for a numeric parameter, this value minus the manual one, as a signed number with its unit; for a categorical parameter such as order, same | differs

inputs.illuminant: recorded with the pass; one k_L or one per illuminant class is pending (photometry-commissioning)
